item.title: Country Music Association Names Brittany Schaffer as Next CEO
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to "Music News"! Today, we're talking about a big change in the country music scene. The Country Music Association has just announced its new CEO, Brittany Schaffer. She'll be taking over for Sarah Trahern, who's retiring after 13 years with the organization.
[Short music transition]
Host: Schaffer will join the CMA on September 8th as part of a strategic transition plan, and will officially become CEO on January 1st, 2027. She's coming from Belmont University, where she was the dean of the Mike Curb College of Entertainment and Music Business. Before that, she spent over a decade as an entertainment attorney and worked with Spotify.
[Short music transition]
Host: The CMA board chairman, Jay Williams, says that Schaffer is the perfect leader to take the organization into its next era. And Schaffer herself is excited to serve the country music community, saying that it's an honor to represent the industry and help connect country music with fans around the world.
[Clip of Brittany Schaffer's quote plays]
Host: Outgoing CEO Sarah Trahern is also welcoming Schaffer to the role, saying that she trusts the search committee's decision and wishes Schaffer every success. Trahern is grateful for her time with the CMA and is looking forward to cheering on the industry in the years to come.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to "Music News"! We'll be back with more updates from the music world soon.
